newsitem.title: UK: BAA says expects to avoid windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: BAA says expects to avoid windfall tax.

text.p: Airport operator BAA Plc on Tuesday continued to insist it did not expect to be the target of a Labour windfall tax on utilities, but fears over the tax sent its shares sharply lower.

"We remain convinced that the tax cannot possibly apply to BAA," said a spokeswoman for the company. "We are not a utility, we are not making excess profits and we are investing heavily in the national network."
The spokeswoman declined comment on whether BAA envisaged any legal challenge to any windfall tax if Labour chose to include it in the tax's net.
Shares in BAA, operator of London's Gatwick and Heathrow airports, were down 13.5p or 2.6 percent at 507-1/2 by 1530 GMT, among the biggest declines in the FTSE 100 index.
Earlier a Labour source had told Reuters the windfall tax was likely to be levied on BAA as well as British Telecommunications Plc.

Labour's economics spokesman Gordon Brown declined to name companies that would be targeted by the levy, intended to fund a job creation and training programme, but said it would be non-discriminatory -- which lawyers said was essential if it were to avoid legal challenge.
